data.name: Argentina
data.summary: Argentina taxes residents on worldwide income. Gains on foreign listed shares are taxed at a flat 15% (Argentine listed shares are exempt); foreign dividends are taxed at the progressive rates up to 35%, with a foreign tax credit. There is no federal inheritance or gift tax (the Province of Buenos Aires has one; the City of Buenos Aires does not). The personal assets tax (Bienes Personales) is a broad wealth tax on worldwide gross assets: 0.5% to 0.75% in 2026, falling to 0.25% from 2027 under Law 27.743. New residents become taxable after 12 months of residence.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Resident individuals pay income tax on worldwide income (5%-35% progressive; schedular 15% on securities gains) and the annual personal assets tax on worldwide assets above the non-taxable minimum. The capital, Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires, levies no inheritance tax.
regimes.eligibility: Foreign individuals residing in Argentina for reasons other than work become tax resident from the 13th month of presence (PwC Residence). A residence permit is needed for non-Mercosur nationals.

capital_gains.summary: Gains of resident individuals on shares, bonds and fund units are taxed at a flat 15% (schedular). Gains on shares traded on a CNV-supervised Argentine market or issued in an IPO, and on Argentine government/corporate bonds and local mutual funds, are exempt. Gains on foreign securities are foreign-source and taxed at 15%. From 1 January 2026 gains on the sale of real estate by resident individuals are exempt (reform effective for transfers on or after 1 Jan 2026).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Gains on digital currencies 15%. Gains computed on foreign securities in foreign currency for foreign-source rules (not verified). Provincial stamp tax (around 1%-1.5%) may apply to some contracts.

open_questions: The 15% rate for foreign-source share gains (LIG art. 94, ex-art. 90 3rd paragraph) is confirmed only by a press article and practitioner consultations, not by the consolidated law text (infoleg page could not be opened).
Whether the 2026 real-estate exemption also covers foreign real estate held by residents is not stated; real_estate_foreign left null.
capital_gains.rate_basis: LIG schedular rate 15% on results from the sale of shares and securities by resident individuals (PwC Income determination; Deloitte 2026); exemption for CNV-listed shares/IPO shares. Foreign listed securities: 15% foreign-source rate. private_business_sale = unlisted shares at 15%. Local real estate exempt for transfers from 1 Jan 2026 (PwC, Significant developments).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Habitual dealers carrying on a business are taxed on business income at progressive rates up to 35%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide; foreign tax credit limited to the Argentine tax on the foreign-source income (PwC Foreign tax relief).

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends are foreign-source income taxed at the general progressive rates (top 35%). Dividends from Argentine companies out of profits from 2018 onwards bear a 7% withholding tax, which is final for individuals.

open_questions: FY2026 brackets are indexed semi-annually; the 35% rate applied above ARS 60,750,914 of semi-annual taxable income for January-June 2026.
dividends.rate_basis: Foreign dividends at the top progressive PIT rate 35% (PwC Taxes on personal income, FY2026 top rate 35%). Domestic dividends: 7% WHT on dividends from 2018+ profits (PwC Income determination; Deloitte 2026). Credit for foreign tax up to the Argentine tax on that income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 7% WHT on dividends to residents and non-residents (profits from 2018 onwards); 35% equalisation tax only on distributions of pre-2018 untaxed earnings. Argentine companies also pay the 0.5% personal assets tax on shares held by individuals as substitute taxpayer.
dividends.treaty_network: About 30 treaties (PwC list includes Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, Qatar, Russia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, UAE, UK; Japan, Luxembourg and China pending). No treaty with the US.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Controlled foreign entities with passive income may be looked through under transparency rules (PwC).

wealth_tax.summary: The Impuesto sobre los Bienes Personales taxes resident individuals on worldwide assets (no deduction for liabilities) above the non-taxable minimum (ARS 384,728,044.57 for FY2025, indexed annually). Law 27.743 sets the 2026 scale at 0.50% up to ARS 13,688,704.13 (2023 base, indexed) and 0.75% above; from 2027 the rate is a flat 0.25%. Argentine bank deposits and government bonds are exempt; the owner-occupied home is exempt up to ARS 1,346,548,155.99 (FY2025).
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Law 27.743 rate path: 2023 0.5%-1.5%, 2024 0.5%-1.25%, 2025 0.5%-1.0%, 2026 0.5%-0.75%, 2027 onwards 0.25%. Individuals working in Argentina for up to five years are taxed only on Argentine assets (requires employment).

components.name: Impuesto sobre los Bienes Personales (FY2026 scale, FY2025 indexed amounts)
components.notes: Base is gross assets (liabilities generally not deductible), so net_wealth_worldwide overstates the deduction. Bracket threshold ARS 52,664,283 is the FY2025 indexed value of the 2023 base ARS 13,688,704.13. Rate falls to 0.25% flat from FY2027 (Law 27.743 art. 25(e)). Foreign wealth taxes on foreign assets are creditable. Argentine shares are taxed at 0.5% via the company (substitute taxpayer), not in the individual's return.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Provincial/municipal real estate tax (e.g. ABL in Buenos Aires City) on fiscal value; 0.6% tax on bank account debits and credits; provincial stamp tax.

inheritance.summary: There is no federal inheritance or gift tax. The Province of Buenos Aires levies a gratuitous transfer tax (Impuesto a la Transmision Gratuita de Bienes) under its own conditions; the City of Buenos Aires (CABA), where the family would most likely live, does not. The JSON scores the CABA position.
inheritance.regional_differences: Province of Buenos Aires (not CABA) levies an inheritance and gift tax; other provinces currently do not (PwC).

inheritance.gift_tax: No federal gift tax; Province of Buenos Aires taxes gifts under its gratuitous-transfer tax.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No national tax on any assets.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Provincial tax depends on domicile in the Province of Buenos Aires / situs there.

residency.tax_residency_test: Foreign nationals become resident from the 13th month of presence in Argentina (for reasons other than work); foreign nationals assigned to work for up to five years remain non-resident. Law 27,802 clarified that citizenship by naturalisation for relevant investments does not by itself make a person tax resident (PwC Residence).

routes.requirements: Nationals of Mercosur and associated states can obtain residence under the Mercosur residence agreement (not researched in detail).

routes.requirements: Temporary residence categories exist for persons with passive income or investments; amounts not researched. A citizenship-by-investment route exists (Law 27,802 reference in PwC) but terms were not researched.

income.name: Argentina

income_tax.summary: Argentine residents pay Ganancias on a progressive scale of 5% to 35% (article 94 scale, values for July-December 2026, indexed twice a year by INDEC CPI). Employees and autonomos get a non-taxable minimum and a special deduction. Employees contribute 17% of salary up to a monthly cap; autonomos pay fixed monthly amounts by category.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Autonomos (general regime) pay a fixed monthly amount by category, not a share of actual income: from 15 January 2026 category I is ARS 62,743.08 (reference income ARS 196,072.13) up to category V ARS 276,065.92 (reference income ARS 862,706.01), i.e. 32% of the reference income in every category (calcularsueldo.com.ar, 19 Jan 2026 page). Category V is the highest, so the contribution stops growing with income: the cap field is category V's reference income x 12 (ARS 10,352,472) and rate 0.32 applies up to it (about ARS 3.31 million a year; on a EUR ~54k income this is a small share of income). Later 2026 category amounts (a prior pass noted ARS 318,759 for category V from mid-June, not re-sourced) are higher, so this slightly understates. Monotributo (simplified) alternative exists but has revenue ceilings and was not researched.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No city-level personal income tax in Buenos Aires; provincial turnover tax (Ingresos Brutos) applies to professionals but is not modelled. Scale and allowances are the July-December 2026 values (the latest ARCA update, 8.42% above the January-June values, taken as the year-end annual scale).

regimes.name: Digital nomad transitory residence (Disposicion 758/2022)
regimes.description: Transitory residence of up to 180 days for foreigners from visa-exempt countries who work remotely for clients or employers abroad; extendable once for the same length. No minimum income is set at application; extension requires income receipts and at least 50% of the period spent in Argentina. It carries no tax benefit; non-working residents become tax resident from the 13th month.
regimes.duration_note: 180 days plus one extension of the same length (about 12 months).
